verdict:
evidence_table at e8f6efb. HEAD 9951713 changes no evidence_table file.

Four frames have changed since r10 (09c4af8):
- purses (3103170) and seam (e8f6efb), both 2560x1440; I read both in detail;
- page, republished at 3c7634e;
- page_foot, new at 688f15e.

The other ten are unchanged. I re-read and measured all fourteen. Mean 5.6, lowest 5 (materials). Not pro level. Scores kept.

The Ch 04 pair has progressed on everything r10 measured:
- The tote is no longer mustard. On purses, the front panel (x1850-2150, y650-850) has a graded median-Lab of (20.9, 5.2, 11.1): hue 65.0 deg, chroma 12.3. Lab of the mean RGB gives 63.4 / 12.2, which confirms Codex's 63.62 / 12.31.
- The raw PNG's blue channel is no longer clipped. The panel median is 13, with 10.6% of pixels below 8 (r10: 92% at 0).
- On open panel, the macro matches the master:
  - x900-1800, y800-1200: h 60.7, C 12.7, L 20.9, dE76 1.03 to purses;
  - x900-1800, y1000-1400: h 64.3, C 12.3, dE76 0.31.
  - Codex's 0.55 falls in that range.
- The bare-leather gaps beside both straps are closed. The row starts at about x 672 against the left strap and ends at about x 2104 against the right.
- The tote's hardware is no longer lime. Ring chroma now peaks at about 19 (r10: 28), at hue about 54.
- The receipt no longer competes. Its graded p95 is 44 against the tote panel's 62.

What still keeps this below a fern film:
1. The macro's stitch row does not read as saddle thread.
   - Each stitch is a near-white sliver over a dark wedge of its own shadow (Y about 30-35 against 54-56 for the leather).
   - Stitch peaks sit at L median 47, p90 59, against leather at L 21-24, with chroma about 7. Taking the brightest pixel in each column along the trace instead gives median 34, p90 53.
   - The frame's brightest pixel is on the row (Y 157 at 734, 710).
   - The row reads as slits or white slashes, and it does not match the cream dashes baked into the tabs in the same frame.
2. The exported trace is a sawtooth.
   - In seam.seam.json it swings around a smooth curve by -4.8 to +5.4 px (2nd-98th percentile), one tooth per stitch (about 54 px). purses.seam.json swings ±0.8 px.
   - gfx/seam.html's own smoothing (Gaussian, sigma 1.5 samples) still leaves about ±4 px, so a red line drawn from it will zigzag.
3. The fittings are subdued in colour but read as chalk.
   - On seam, the tote's rings are blotchy white-grey putty (Y p99 about 133 left, 140 right), not brass.
   - On purses, the satchel's clasp and handle rings are off-white plastic. The clasp peaks at about 120 at (1259, 843), second only to the tote's left edge (127 at 1637, 930).
4. The receipt is quieter but no longer reads as paper. It is cold grey (median Lab L about 7, b about -1) with a heavy roll shadow, and the flat tail reads as a grey card.
5. The seam frame's brightest area is the left strap's lit face. About 22,000 of the frame's 24,600 pixels at 120 or above are on it. The face is pale pink-beige (L 53, hue 44 against the panel's 61) and reads as vinyl.
6. The olive smudge behind the lip remains at (1300-1360, 580-605): hue about 78, chroma 7.
7. The macro panel has no leather grain. High-pass std is about 0.5, which is noise only. There is also a dark speck at (907, 876), about 15 levels below its surround, and a matching one on purses at (1752, 812), about 12 below.
8. The purses master is the dimmest frame in the stage.
   - Luma p99 is about 70 (seam 107, push 164, page 190), p50 is 9, and about 46% of pixels are below 8.
   - The tote, the chapter's hero, peaks at a panel p95 of 62.
   - The satchel body is still black (p50 16).

Highest-priority structural issue across the sequence: Ch 04 asks one generated mesh with one material to hold up in a 63 mm macro. handbag-tote.glb is confirmed as 1 mesh, 1 primitive and 1 material.
- Every macro fault above is a patch on that asset: the lip normal retouch, ray-cast stitches, a metallic-mask hardware tint, texel paint-overs, the olive blob, the chalky rings, the lumpy lip and the strap's vinyl sheen.
- Ten rounds of critique have moved the numbers but not the read.
- The fix is a procedural hero front for the seam camera, parented to the tote: panel, rolled lip, tabs, straps and rings, with their own leather, brass and thread materials, and stitches seated in punched holes. The alternative is to reframe the macro to a magnification the asset can hold.

Secondary sequence issue: two graphics plates have lifted floors.
- page_foot and pair: p1 20 and 12, p5 26 and 20. The noir masters sit at purses 2 / 3 and push 1.6 / 2.6. (The plates' p50, 113 and 68, is mostly paper area, so the floor is the fair measure.)
- page's floor is normal (p1 5.5).
- Bring their wood down in the render, with a tighter lamp falloff or less fill on the boards. Do not use a different grade: DECISIONS fixes grade A. Otherwise they will cut as a different film.

Other frames:
- push, passport and laptop/laptop_before remain the strongest. The republished page is clean.
- entries and motifs still show white scratch streaks on the wood, and tickets fainter ones. page_foot has faint ones too (about x 565-720, y 890-1050), and its wood grain reads smeared at 2560.
- overhead's lamp shade reads black and push's white-grey, but both are the same desk-lamp asset. Push sees the pale reflector inside in three-quarter view; overhead sees the dark enamel top. No action.

Process: no issue. 0fe8551 edits noir-kit/props.py. coordination/README.md assigns noir-kit/*.py to Codex as the kit owner, and that contract overrides AGENT_BRIEF.md's stage-agent rule.
answers:
1. Purses master and seam macro, tote colour (D65 Lab, sRGB JPEG)
- Purses, x1850-2150 y650-850:
  - median of per-pixel Lab: L 20.85, h 64.98, C 12.27;
  - Lab of the median RGB: 63.12 / 11.79;
  - Lab of the mean RGB: 63.37 / 12.21.
  - Codex's 63.62 / 12.31 is confirmed.
- Hue is on target. Chroma is 0.7 under the 13-14 floor.
- In the raw PNG, the panel's median RGB is (106, 54, 13), and only 10.6% of pixels have blue below 8 (0.4% at 0). The sat clip is gone. The graded panel has blue median 35.
- On seam, the same pixel box is the wrong place to measure. On the macro it holds the right strap's edge and the stitch row, and gives h 54.5, C 13.5, dE76 2.7.
- On open panel the seam macro matches:
  - x900-1800, y800-1200: h 60.7, C 12.7, L 20.85, dE76 1.03;
  - x900-1800, y1000-1400: h 64.3, C 12.3, dE76 0.31.
  - Codex's 0.55 sits inside that range. The match passes.
- Read: the tote is no longer mustard. At L 21 and C 12 under the warm key it reads camel or tan more than deep cognac. Pushing chroma to about 13.5 at the same hue would help. Both plates pass the numeric gate.

2. The thread beside both strap edges (seam)
- Fixed.
- In seam.seam.json:
  - occluded_x_px is [472-670] and [2106-2298];
  - the visible sidecar runs are 0-471, 671-2104 and 2299-2560 (the sidecar is clipped to the frame).
- seam_paths_px in seam.corners.json runs off-frame: -490 to 470, 673 to 2098 and 2300 to 3219.
- On the frame, stitches start at about x 672 against the left strap's inner edge and end at about x 2104 against the right strap. No visible span runs over bare leather.
- Two new problems:
  a) The sidecar trace follows each stitch's slant and snaps back.
     - Against a 25-sample moving mean, the residual is -4.8 to +5.4 px (2nd-98th percentile), one tooth per stitch (about 54 px, 18 samples).
     - Purses is ±0.8 px.
     - gfx/seam.html's smoothSeam (Gaussian, sigma 1.5 samples) still leaves about ±4 px, so the red trace will zigzag. r10 fix 3.4 asked for it to stay smooth.
  b) The row reads as white slits rather than thread:
     - per-stitch graded peaks are L median 47, p10 33, p90 59; the per-column maximum along the trace is median 34, p90 53;
     - the leather is L 21-24, and the crowns' chroma is about 7;
     - a stitch crown holds the frame's brightest pixel (Y 157 at 734, 710);
     - each crown has a dark shadow wedge beside it (Y about 30-35 against leather 54-56), from the 'tote lip graze' light;
     - the thread colour (0.30, 0.20, 0.11) is lost to the graze;
     - the tabs in the same frame carry baked cream dashes, so the frame has two different kinds of stitching.
- Purses: the row is continuous and faint outside the tab intervals (1835-1871 and 2111-2147), which is acceptable at plate scale.

3. The subdued fittings
- Colour is fixed. On seam, the tote's ring chroma is p95 about 14-17 and max about 19, at hue about 54. There is no lime.
- But they read as chalk:
  - the rings' lit faces are blotchy white-grey putty (L about 43-47, chroma 7.5, Y p99 about 133 left and 140 right) with a dark slot, not aged brass;
  - there is a small dark-green fleck at about (650, 825) on the left strap's inner ring.
- On purses:
  - the satchel's clasp, top rings and side clip are pale grey-white plastic (clasp Lab chroma about 3);
  - the clasp has a melted, crumpled form;
  - the clasp peaks at about 120 at (1259, 843), the frame's second-brightest point after the tote's left edge (127 at 1637, 930);
  - the tote's feet are low-chroma pinkish grey (hue about 37-49, chroma 5-7).
- The olive smudge above the trace's centre is still there: (1300-1360, 580-605), hue 77.6, chroma 7.4.

4. The receipt under the table lamp (purses)
- Value is fixed:
  - roll: p95 about 44, max about 47;
  - flat tail: p95 about 20;
  - the tote panel's p95 is 62, so the receipt is more than 15 below it.
- Identity is lost. It is cold neutral grey: the roll is Lab L about 13 and the tail about 5, with b about -1 and chroma under 3. The roll still reads as a rolled sheet, but the flat tail, under the roll's heavy shadow, reads as a grey card, not thermal paper.
- For Ch 04 it must still read as a receipt: paper-white with a slight warmth, kept dark only by the light falloff.

5. Score, and the highest-priority structural issue
- Scores: composition 6, lighting 5.5, materials 5, set dressing 5.5, grounding/scale 6, cast (staged absence) 6, story read 5.5, technical 5.5. Mean 5.6. Not pro level.
- Structural issue: Ch 04's hero shot depends on a generated single-mesh, single-material tote (handbag-tote.glb: 1 mesh, 1 material), shot at 63 mm and f/6.3 from about 0.37 m.
  - Each remaining macro defect comes from that asset or from patching it: the chalk rings, the lumpy lip creases above the row, the olive texel blob, the pink-vinyl strap sheen, the absent grain, and ray-cast stitch tubes standing proud of the surface with shadow wedges.
  - Build the macro's subject procedurally (fix 1), or reframe the insert to a magnification the GLB holds.
- Second structural issue: tonal continuity.
  - page_foot and pair have lifted floors: p1 20 and 12, p5 26 and 20.
  - The noir masters are deep: purses p1 2, push 1.6. page's floor is normal (p1 5.5).
  - The purses master peaks at luma p99 about 70, the dimmest highlight in the stage.
  - Lower the plates' wood in the render, not with a different grade (grade A is fixed).

fixes.fix:
1. In a new scenes/stages/evidence_table_tote.py, build a 'tote hero front'. Parent it to the tote holder and make it visible only for seam (hide_render elsewhere, as with 'tote lip graze'). It has these parts:
   a. A panel slab about 0.30 x 0.20 m and 2.5 mm thick, sitting 0.3 mm proud of the GLB face along the existing ray-cast surface. It has a rolled lip: a 4 mm-radius half-cylinder along the top edge, bevel 3 segments.
   b. Two tabs, pentagon outline about 34 x 46 mm and 3 mm thick, with a 1 mm bevel and their own edge-paint strip (darker, about 0.6 x leather). Give them the same thread spline as the hem, so the frame has one stitch language.
   c. Straps as swept curves: a rounded-rectangle profile 14 x 4 mm following the GLB strap path.
   d. D-rings as torus segments (major radius 9 mm, minor radius 1.6 mm).
2. Materials:
   - leather: base (0.26, 0.11, 0.045), roughness 0.55, spec 0.3, pebble bump at 0.4 mm with strength 0.12, plus a 2 cm value variation of ±6%;
   - brass: (0.36, 0.22, 0.09), metallic about 0.5, roughness 0.45. Check that it does not go black in this dark room (see fix 4).
3. Punch the row's needle holes as 0.6 mm dimples, and seat the thread spline 0.1 mm into them (see fix 2).
4. Match the purses panel Lab within dE 2 at x900-1800, y800-1200.
5. If this is too much for one pass, pull CAMERAS['seam'] back instead (lens 63 to 45, or loc 4-5 cm further out), so the GLB is never magnified beyond the scale where its texture holds.

fixes.problem:
The thread reads as white slits.
- Per-stitch graded peaks are L median 47, p90 59; the per-column maximum along the trace is median 34, p90 53.
- The leather is L 21-24, and the crowns' chroma is about 7.
- A crown holds the frame's brightest pixel (Y 157 at 734, 710).
- Each stitch has a dark shadow wedge (Y about 30-35 against leather 54-56).
- The row speaks a different stitch language from the tabs' baked dashes.

The exported trace in seam.seam.json is a sawtooth.
- It swings -4.8 to +5.4 px (2nd-98th percentile) around a 25-sample moving mean, one tooth per stitch (about 54 px, 18 samples).
- The cause: _sample_tote_trace interpolates between every control point, slanted stitch ends included.
- purses.seam.json swings ±0.8 px.
- gfx/seam.html's smoothSeam (Gaussian, sigma 1.5 samples) still leaves about ±4 px.
fixes.fix:
1. In project_tote_seam (kit) or a stage-side wrapper, feed _sample_tote_trace only the middle control point of each 3-point stitch spline. Alternatively, smooth the sampled y with a centred moving average one stitch pitch wide (18 samples, about 54 px) before writing 'seam'.
2. Recompute the occluded flags, then check that occluded_x_px still ends at the strap edges (about 470/672 and 2104/2299). With centre-only controls, the run ends can move by up to half a stitch.
3. Acceptance:
   - the residual against a 25-sample moving mean stays within ±1 px on seam;
   - seam_paths_px uses the same centres.

fixes.problem:

The receipt now passes on value (roll p95 about 44, flat tail about 20), but reads as cold grey (median Lab L about 7, b about -1). The flat tail under the roll's heavy shadow reads as a grey card, not thermal paper.
fixes.fix:
1. Warm and lift receipt_stock modestly: from mt.thermal('receipt under the evidence lamp', (0.053, 0.054, 0.057), spec=0.16) to about (0.072, 0.068, 0.060), with spec 0.25 for the slight thermal sheen.
   - A jump to 0.12 would be about 2.3x (+1.2 stops) and would put the roll near p95 65, above the tote panel's 62.
2. If more paper read is needed, move RECEIPT_C4 toward the camera, further into the front cutter's shade (e.g. (0.19, -0.38, 73.0)), and lift the stock again. Keep:
   - roll p95 at 50 or less (still at least 10 under the tote panel);
   - hue slightly warm (b +1 to +3).
3. Shorten the curl radius so the roll's cast shadow covers under half the flat tail's length.

fixes.fix:
1. First render seam with 'tote lip graze' off to confirm that the graze, not the lamp key, lights the strap face.
2. If it is the graze, add a camera-invisible shadow_card (e.g. 0.03 x 0.10 m) between 'tote lip graze' and the left strap.
   - Narrowing the graze's receivers will not help: strap, lip and panel are one GLB mesh, so they enter or leave the receiver collection together.
3. Raise tote rough_add from 0.32 to about 0.40 so the strap highlight broadens and drops. This is shared with purses, so re-check the panel match (dE76 at most 2).
4. Targets:
   - left strap p95 no more than 15 above the panel's p95 (55), so at most about 70;
   - hue 55-65.
